To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the impact of carbon price on supply chain performance is significant and the scope of reduction in total cost and emission by increasing carbon price increases with the increase in cycle service level and the demand coefficient of variation.

cycle service level has a significant impact on total cost and total emission irrespective of the level of demand variability and the scope of carbon emission reduction by increasing the carbon price is greater when demand variability is higher and the service level constraint is more stringent.

increasing cycle service level and variability of demand coefficient of variation increases total cost, total inventory, total emissions, and carbon cost and the scope of reduction of total cost and total emissions by increasing carbon price increases with cycle service level and coefficient of variation of demand.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the inventory lot sizing with non stationary stochastic demand and carbon emission and cycle service constraints under carbon cap and trade policy.

a non stationary stochastic lot sizing problem with service level and emission constraints in a carbon trading system and the results provide insights into the effects of different factors on the total cost, inventory, emission and cycle service levels in such systems.
the inventory lot sizing in supply chain under non stationary stochastic demands with emission and cycle based service level constraints considering the carbon cap and trade mechanism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
increasing carbon price reduces supply chain total cost, total inventory and total emission.
the proposed model and solution methodology is a valuable tool to supply chain decision makers for making decisions under carbon emission regulatory mechanisms.

the supply chain manager should take into account the emission and service level considerations in inventory lot sizing decisions and also the carbon cap and trade mechanism should be implemented with caution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this paper is the first to investigate the impact of emission and service level parameters on the performance of a non stationary stochastic inventory lot size problem in a supply chain under carbon cap and trade mechanism.

the supply chain performance in terms of cost, inventory and emission is highly sensitive to cycle service level and the demand coefficient of variation while the impact of demand pattern is insignificant.

our results provide a good understanding of the effects of emission and service level parameters on supply chain performance and help the supply chain managers in taking right decisions in different demand and emission scenarios.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the supply chain managers can reduce total cost by increasing carbon price but it may not be the case for all situations.
the supply chain managers should consider the demand variability while making emission reduction decisions.
the carbon emission can be reduced by improving the cycle service level.
